summary: DataX is an interactive web app that uses NASA Earth science data to show how local air temperatures have changed and how those trends can inform early-stage data center siting. Users can open one of 32 ready-to-view regional reports in Finland and Canada or select a point on the map for analysis. Each report shows historical temperatures, the rate of change in degrees Celsius per decade, and the uncertainty around that estimate. Users can compare up to three locations within the selected country and see how cooling conditions, solar and wind resources, and water indicators contribute to a site screening score. This helps users identify locations for further assessment.
details:
DataX takes users from a 3D globe to an interactive map of Finland or Canada. Users can open one of 19 Finnish or 13 Canadian regional reference reports, select a point on land for coordinate-based analysis, and compare up to three locations within the selected country on a common chart scale.

The default historical period is 2005–2024. We use monthly NASA POWER data, with MERRA-2 for near-surface air temperature and wind and CERES for solar irradiation. We account for seasonality when estimating temperature trends and use Newey–West standard errors to account for autocorrelation. Reports show the trend in degrees Celsius per decade, a 95% confidence interval, and a significance test. The Finnish regional results also adjust for multiple testing. Users can view an illustrative temperature scenario that extends the fitted historical trend.

DataX applies this analysis to preliminary data center siting. The screening score combines cooling conditions (25%), wind and solar resources (60%), and modeled water indicators (15%). The app shows how each factor contributes to the score, helping users compare trade-offs and shortlist locations for further engineering and environmental assessment.

We built DataX with JavaScript, React, and Next.js. Three.js powers the globe, Chart.js renders the reports and comparisons, and a Python pipeline prepares the bundled Finnish datasets.
